Project File 02 / Research in Progress

VIGIL —
check what matters.

Vulnerability-Adaptive In-Core Guarded Instruction Lane · Selective temporal checking on SonicBOOMv3 RISC-V core.

Chipyard · SonicBOOM · RV64GC ● Full M0 baseline regression: In review
01 / Motivation
02 / Mechanism
03 / Current evidence
04 / The blocker

Why this question?

Temporal redundancy can detect transient faults by comparing work performed at different times. Duplicating every instruction incurs severe power and IPC overhead; checking only vulnerable work could drastically reduce that penalty if classification and recovery mechanisms are reliable.

Proposed mechanism

The current specification describes a four-class Architectural Vulnerability Factor (AVF) classifier, a single-issue shadow lane, commit-time comparison, and hybrid branch/fault-checkpoint recovery. It defines a minimum ROB extension and an eight-entry checkpoint ring.

Core research question: Can selective checking lower the cost of temporal redundancy without compromising error detection latency or architectural recovery?

What has been tested

Isolated checker units passed: the JAL checker unit was 7/7 and the comparator unit was 2/2. These are unit checks only; they do not yet establish that the SonicBOOM microarchitecture integration is closure-ready.

What is not yet established

The full M0 regression is not cleared. A previous run encountered an ELF/runtime mismatch, and runtime status remains inconclusive. There is no finished end-to-end reliability claim until the baseline stabilizes.

Next gate

Reproduce the pinned RV64GC baseline, clear the regression, and compare the guarded core against an unmodified baseline under controlled fault injections to report coverage, timing, and area trade-offs.
